solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Left-overs to arrange, starter coming last

indicators.note: the word's opening letter is moved from the front to the back

parts.note: to sort is to arrange

explanation.surface: Instructions for tidying the scraps from a meal, leaving the first course till the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' tempts you to think of a first course, which suits the left-overs, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps of food left over after a meal, an old literary word.

clue.text: Bits of rocky ornamentation, Japanese, in garden design

indicators.note: small bits of each word means just their leading letters

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Pieces of rockwork decorating a Japanese-style garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a fair description of the thing defined, which is why the initials fit so neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A roji is the stepping-stone garden path leading to a Japanese tea house, a style of garden layout.

clue.text: Young girl holding knot of ribbon up, cheap in US

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top
one thing holding another has it inside

parts.note: tit is an old word for a girl or young woman
a bow is a knot tied in a ribbon

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a ribbon bow in her hair, described as tacky by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit as a girl is an old usage; today it usually means the bird. Two bits was a quarter dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is American slang for worthless or cheap, from the old value of a quarter dollar.

clue.text: Mine prop right inside passages seen from below

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards means backwards
one letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: gaps are openings or passages
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pit prop placed in the tunnels, viewed by someone underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passages seen from below' suits the mine scene, but the passages are gaps read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprag is a short wooden prop used to support a mine roof or a coal seam.

clue.text: Monoxide of a kind? Charm incorporates reverse of it

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body of another

parts.note: a mascot is a lucky charm

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry riddle about an oxide, followed by a remark about a lucky token.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this is one specific monoxide, of lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Massicot is yellow lead monoxide, used as a pigment, so it is one particular monoxide.

clue.text: Volcanic feature, form of mound, one-third pumice, after eruption

indicators.note: a new form of something is a reshaping of it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is two of its letters, here the final pair

parts.note: the last third of this word

explanation.surface: Describing a volcano's aftermath: a heap of debris partly made of pumice.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes MOUND plus the final third of pumice, CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mud cone is a small conical hill built up by a mud volcano or geyser, a landform found in volcanic areas.

clue.text: Duck when catching book? This may detect visual defects

indicators.note: catching something means holding it within

parts.note: a scoter is a sea duck
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A duck snatching a book, and a hint at some optical testing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' could be a verb or a cricket score of nought; here it is a sea bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A scotometer is an instrument for mapping blind spots, or scotomata, in the field of vision.

clue.text: What's analogous to alcohol? Some components extracted in this school

indicators.note: taking out some of the parts leaves only what remains

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher asking what compares with alcohol, then mentioning extracting parts in the school lab.
explanation.walkthrough: From THIS SCHOOL the middle letters SSCHO are pulled out, leaving THI and OL.
explanation.definitionFit: A thiol is the sulphur counterpart of an alcohol, with sulphur replacing the oxygen of the hydroxyl group.

clue.text: Old nag having short run within grasp no longer

indicators.note: within places one item inside another

parts.note: caple or capul is an archaic word for a horse
R is the abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An aged horse with little running left in it, no longer able to keep its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the definition as an obsolete word, from Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Craple is an obsolete Spenserian word meaning to grapple or claw, so it is an archaic verb for grasp.

clue.text: With respect to fee paid, pound included not connected

parts.note: of can mean concerning or about

indicators.note: something included is put inside the rest

parts.note: a fine is a sum paid as a penalty
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone discussing a fee, with a pound added, who then loses their connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The L sits inside the second word, after its first letter, splitting the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Offline describes a device or person not linked to a network or the internet.

clue.text: Tiresomely precocious kid, eager, went off the rails

indicators.note: going off the rails means going wildly wrong and out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A precocious child, too keen by half, who then misbehaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child of about ten to twelve, often seen as acting older than their age.

clue.text: Blow received in ruck? That'll be a buckeroo

indicators.note: something received in another is taken into it

parts.note: ruck is a dialect verb meaning to crouch or cower
a punch is a blow

explanation.surface: A punch landing in a rugby ruck, hinting at a cowboy's rough life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruck' looks like the rugby scrum, but here it is the dialect verb to crouch.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckeroo is American slang for a cowboy, and a cowpuncher is a cattle-herding cowboy.

clue.text: Long arm in car protecting judge

indicators.note: something protecting another surrounds it

parts.note: Ford is a make of car
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge sheltered inside a car with a long reach.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes inside FORD after F. 'Long arm' suggests the long arm of the law, but it is an arm of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fjord is a long, narrow inlet of the sea between steep cliffs, an arm of water reaching inland.

clue.text: House plant, large: one sags from below, stair disturbed

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from below means upwards, so backwards
something disturbed has been thrown into disorder

parts.note: to dip is to sag
the five letters of stair rearranged

explanation.surface: A big pot plant drooping on a staircase that has been knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then DIPS reversed to SPID, then STAIR rearranged as ISTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a tough, broad-leaved plant long popular indoors, famously large and hard to kill.

clue.text: Diner some defaced from back to front

indicators.note: reading from the back to the front runs the letters the other way
some of a word is just a part of its letters

parts.note: the run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A vandalised restaurant, with its sign spoiled from rear to front.
explanation.walkthrough: EFAC sits inside defaced; read backwards it gives CAFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is an informal eating place, which is what a cafe is.

clue.text: Congenital condition, generally avoided: suffering in gloom's medium

indicators.note: suffering words are damaged and put out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
the apostrophe is ignored
M is the abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A description of a gloomy medium, a spiritualist in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally avoided' is part of the definition: the term is now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongolism is a dated, now offensive name for Down's syndrome, a genetic condition present from birth.

clue.text: Plug giving tip after show's opening

indicators.note: one part is placed following the other in order
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of show
to tip over is to topple

explanation.surface: Advice given at the start of a performance, like a hint passed to an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopple is a stopper or bung that closes the mouth of a vessel.

clue.text: Only a few compete in it, swimming in oily gloop

definitions.text: Only a few compete in it

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A race where just a few contestants wade through sticky slime.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligopoly is a market controlled by a small number of sellers, so competition is limited.

clue.text: Prat abandoning European supporters of home rule

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it out

parts.note: prat is slang for the buttocks, and nates is the anatomical word
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A fool walking out on Europe to back self-government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prat' reads as a fool, but here it is the old word for the backside. NATES loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nats is a short informal name for nationalists, such as Scottish nationalists who seek self-rule.

clue.text: Jellyfish that is core of jelly quivering in luminous glow

indicators.note: the shaken group goes inside the other word

parts.note: an aura is a glowing light around something

indicators.note: quivering letters shake into a new order

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the core is the central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of jelly

explanation.surface: A jellyfish quivering and glowing in the dark water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly' tempts you towards the definition, but only its centre letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurelia is a genus of jellyfish, including the common moon jelly.

clue.text: Man embarrassed about poetic effort, bright red

indicators.note: an embarrassed word is flustered and thrown into disarray
about means going around something

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: A man blushing scarlet over his attempt at verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The red blush of embarrassment fits the surface neatly, so the definition seems part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Modena is a deep crimson or purplish red colour, named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Countryman's bird? Do please let it out

parts.note: O is the exclamation of pleading, as in 'O, do!'
to vent something is to let it out

explanation.surface: A plea to release a bird kept indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'O, vent it!', an urgent request. 'Countryman's' marks a dialect name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven tit is a rural name for a willow warbler or similar bird that builds a domed, oven-shaped nest.

clue.text: Was stuffing left out? Very disappointed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having the innards removed, as a fish or bird is

explanation.surface: A cook who forgot the stuffing for the turkey, and is crushed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a cryptic question: something with its insides taken out has had its stuffing left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutted means with the entrails removed, and colloquially means bitterly let down.

clue.text: Foreign rabbit, indulged, tucked into exotic fish

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside

parts.note: tai is a Japanese sea bream
to pet is to pamper or indulge

explanation.surface: A pampered pet rabbit fed on exotic fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tai, a Japanese sea bream, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapeti is a wild rabbit of Central and South America.

clue.text: Northerner's clever, adding gallons to pin

indicators.note: adding one thing to another joins them in sequence

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for gallons
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A clever northern engineer adding fuel gauges to a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northerner's' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleg is Scots for quick-witted or sharp, so a northern word for smart.

clue.text: Liable to change

indicators.note: change means alter the order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition while also giving an anagram of its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Labile means unstable or apt to alter, especially in chemistry and psychology.

clue.text: Clownish slap we stand up to, absorbing blow

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside

parts.note: taken as written
a hit is a blow
to face an opponent is to stand up to them

explanation.surface: A slapstick routine in which we confront someone and take a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' looks like a strike, but it is theatre slang for makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiteface is the white greasepaint of a clown, and slap is stage makeup.

clue.text: Routine, broad imposition

parts.note: broad and ho are both American slang for a woman
hum is an old word for a hoax or imposition

explanation.surface: A dull routine, imposed widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad' looks like an adjective, but it is the US slang noun for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum describes something dull, ordinary and unremarkable.

clue.text: University initially limited in money, providing unacceptable service?

indicators.note: the pair goes inside the other word

parts.note: fat is slang for money or profit
U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of limited

explanation.surface: A university short of funds offering a poor service to its students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is meant in the tennis sense, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a fault is a serve that does not land in the correct court, so it is disallowed.

clue.text: Scaly eels wriggling round loose fish?

indicators.note: wriggling letters twist into a new order
round means surrounding something

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
a loose fish is a dissolute person, here a prostitute, PRO

explanation.surface: Scaly eels writhing around a fish that has got free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose fish' is an old phrase for a person of loose morals, not a fish at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Leprose is a botanical and zoological word meaning scurfy or covered in scales.

clue.text: Fellows turning up in highland trim

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upward means reading in the opposite direction

parts.note: dons are college fellows

explanation.surface: University fellows arriving neatly dressed in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highland' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snod is a Scots adjective meaning neat or tidy, as is trim.

clue.text: Number one dictionary (shorter), an evergreen

indicators.note: making something shorter means cutting part of it away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a lexicon is a dictionary

explanation.surface: Recommending the best short dictionary for looking up an evergreen tree.
explanation.walkthrough: LEXICON is cut short to LEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holly genus, and also the holm oak, both of which keep their leaves all year.

clue.text: Massage therapy auntie endlessly applied

indicators.note: applied here means worked on and reshaped
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aunt giving a massage treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE without its last letter is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuina is a Chinese therapeutic massage, related to acupressure.

clue.text: Whirlwind outing with notification of what's owed in advance

parts.note: a tour is an outing
a bill states what you owe
on means ahead or forward

explanation.surface: A whirlwind trip whose bill arrives before you set off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourbillon is a whirlwind or swirling vortex, from the French word.

clue.text: Mum attending matins properly dressed, a regular flag-flyer

indicators.note: dressed means set in order, so the letters are rearranged
attending means going alongside, placing one next to the other

parts.note: ma is mother
the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother going to morning service in her Sunday best, a regular churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' plays on dressing a ship with flags. 'Regular' is a hint, a flag-flyer that is always present.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainmast is a ship's principal mast, from which flags are commonly flown.

clue.text: Nursery favourite losing half of stuffing, tiresome for Walter

indicators.note: losing half means one of the two matching letters is dropped

parts.note: a teddy bear is a favourite nursery toy
the stuffing is the middle of the word, its double D

explanation.surface: A worn teddy bear losing its stuffing, now just a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: TEDDY loses one of its middle Ds. Walter is Sir Walter Scott, whose Scots usage gives this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedy is a Scots form of tedious, so a word for dull used by Scott.
